I’ll use GPT-6 Astra at xhigh for the offline audit, inspect the referenced evidence and concrete sources, and write only the requested concise `cost-audit.md`.

I’m applying the xTS evidence skill to keep frozen measurements, current candidates, and pending board acceptance distinct. Root retains exclusive hardware ownership; this audit will use local files only.

The IOB increase has a concrete cost: 52,736 bytes of internal RAM. E69’s 32k and 64k socket tests both used IOB256, so those results do not establish that IOB128 would preserve throughput. Network budget cuts remain conditional on Root’s same-AP baseline.

Two changes appear worth keeping: E75 reuses an already-read Flash status, and E84 removes a redundant seek without enlarging buffers. The VFS cache does carry a real cost: up to 256 KiB of PSRAM shared globally, plus metadata. I’m checking its commit and shared-handle behavior before recommending a smaller cap.

The audit will distinguish limits from allocated memory: reducing a socket window does not reclaim the fixed IOB array, and the 256 KiB VFS pool is an on-demand global cap, not a per-file allocation. The filesystem checks will also include close time and flag extra COW work that a smaller pool could trigger.

E88’s host evidence shows less copying—61,140 to 1,490 bytes in the near-full case—with a tradeoff of at most one additional existing 412-byte IOB held per nonempty socket. That makes it relevant to slow UDP RX, but it has no board throughput result yet and should be evaluated separately from pool cuts.

The remaining small-read gap points to service overhead: FS06 B’s 1000 reads took 57.581 ms, and its FILE/fd replays improved without Flash I/O. The ready `korvo-fs-read-service` diagnostic is the next focused step to separate cached VFS work from the remaining call overhead before changing RAM budgets.
More precisely, FILE replay improved; fd replay stayed around 40.8 ms. Both had zero Flash I/O increments, which is why larger buffers are not yet justified.
The decision table is written. I’m checking its source links and acceptance conditions, especially where a proposed cut only lowers a cap or still depends on the pending same-AP baseline.

The source links check out. I’m shortening the verification detail into the decision table and adding the ordinary LittleFS cache cost per file and per mount, separately from the global dirty-page pool.
